settings.heading: Three ways to establish
settings.description: Start with the agreed program scope, then choose the commercial model that suits how your organisation wants to own, fund and coordinate it.

settings.heading: How large is the workforce?
settings.text: We look at workforce size, operational coverage, contractor groups and whether the program must work across different shifts.

settings.heading: How many sites are involved?
settings.text: Locations, shift patterns and geographic spread influence equipment, training, servicing and the level of coordination required.

settings.heading: How often will testing occur?
settings.text: Current or expected testing frequency helps determine device capacity, consumables, servicing and ongoing support.

settings.heading: Where and when will testing happen?
settings.text: Roles, operating environments and testing triggers help shape suitable methods, devices and procedures.

settings.heading: Who runs the program today?
settings.text: We look at who currently owns policy, testing, records and reviews, and where additional capability may be needed.

settings.heading: How would you prefer to fund the program?
settings.text: The agreed scope may use a direct purchase, recurring agreement or broader managed coordination. Final availability and terms require a proposal.

settings.heading: How does the compliance review work?
settings.text: We begin by understanding your policy, roles, sites, testing methods, equipment, training, collection and chain-of-custody steps, records and escalation process. You then receive a prioritised view of capability gaps and practical next steps. It is a program review, not a legal audit or legal advice.
